units.function: Focused route tests for plugin-scoped HTTP dispatch, authentication modes, company resolution, checkout policy, worker readiness and header filtering.
units.dependencyDirection: Exercises the production Express router with mocked registry, lifecycle, worker and surrounding services; the route remains the authorization and envelope owner.
units.keyDataModels: Manifest-declared route, auth mode, company scope source, checkout policy, sanitized HTTP envelope and worker response.
units.lifecycle: Registers a ready plugin, dispatches board or Agent requests, applies route/company/checkout checks, forwards to worker and normalizes response headers.
units.testAssessment: Nine focused cases passed after an escalated local-port rerun; the initial sandbox run failed only because listen was denied. Coverage proves header stripping, manifest route exclusion, worker state and several run checks, but explicitly accepts peer-Agent checkout bypass and omits cross-company ordinary members, response bounds, timeout, cancellation and idempotency.
units.designRationale: Expose plugin-owned endpoints under a host namespace without giving plugins direct access to the host HTTP server or inbound authorization credentials.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS Connectors need a narrow ingress/extension envelope with stable tenant and actor binding, payload limits and auditable execution ownership.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the table-driven boundary tests and negative-header assertions, adding ordinary-user and cross-tenant cases, exact run/assignment ownership, response limits, stable error codes, timeout/cancel and idempotency.
units.responsibilityConflict: A test deliberately permits a peer Agent to invoke a route labeled required-for-agent-in-progress without checkout ownership, so the suite codifies a weaker responsibility boundary than Company OS permits.
evidence: 2026-08-18 focused Vitest: 9 passed after sandbox listen EPERM and escalated local-port rerun

units.function: Single Express router for plugin listing, installation, lifecycle, configuration and Secrets, UI bridge and streams, scoped APIs, tools, jobs, webhooks, trusted local folders, health, logs and dashboard diagnostics.
units.dependencyDirection: Imports database schema and queries, authentication assertions, registry/lifecycle/loader, worker RPC, tool gateway, Secret service, job scheduler, local filesystem inspection, activity/live events and UI metadata directly into one 3140-line application boundary.
units.keyDataModels: Plugin record and manifest, instance/company config, Secret reference binding, tool run context, UI bridge envelope, scoped API declaration, job/run, webhook delivery, local-folder grant and health projection.
units.lifecycle: Installs and upgrades packages, starts/stops workers, mutates company config, dispatches synchronous RPC and public webhooks, exposes SSE, records jobs/webhooks and aggregates diagnostics.
units.testAssessment: Scoped API tests pass 9/9, but route-wide negative coverage is incomplete. Webhook authenticity/tenant/replay/retention, local-folder authority, cross-company dashboards, config transactionality, SSE recovery/backpressure and lifecycle concurrency lack proof in the inspected focused suite.
units.designRationale: Offer one public management and runtime surface around the plugin subsystem while keeping worker code behind RPC and manifest declarations.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs equivalent extension operations, but split into explicit administration, tenant configuration, Connector execution, external ingress and diagnostics boundaries governed by human responsibility and data authorization.
units.companyOsFit: REJECT the module as reusable code. ADAPT only narrow primitives: canonical local-path checks, explicit company binding, request/response header allowlists, request size limits, stable categorical RPC errors and raw-body preservation for verified signatures.
units.responsibilityConflict: Manifest declaration acts as authority; peer Agents can bypass protected checkout; instance mutations are copied into every company audit stream; public webhooks persist unverified full payloads and headers without tenant identity; board members can inspect and persist arbitrary host paths; global dashboards can expose cross-company operational errors. None binds high-risk effects to an accountable human, approved purpose, exact data contract and evidence chain.
evidence: 2026-08-18 focused Vitest: 9 passed after sandbox listen EPERM and escalated local-port rerun
